title.en: What tariffs will really cost Canadians and Americans
title.zh: 哪些关税真正会让加拿大人和美国人付出代价

summary.en: Households and businesses have become used to tariffs impacting the cost of living for more than year now, so what will change now?
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
A raft of new tariffs have been announced during the latest escalation of the trade war between the US and Canada.

The North American neighbours have been locked in a bitter economic conflict since US President Donald Trump launched his flagship trade policy on his return to the White House.

This week saw the latest move by the Canadians with Prime Minister Mark Carney imposing retaliatory import taxes on a host of US goods, after Trump threatened hikes of his own.

As the dust settles in this tit-for-tat tariff row, what will be affected most on both sides of the border?

If Trump's threat to raise tariffs on Canadian vehicles from 25% to 50% from 1 January 2027 becomes a reality, then that would deal a further blow to the automotive industry.

Cars, trucks and parts are among the main goods traded between the US, Canada and Mexico, with the manufacturing sector and supply chains stretching across borders.

Despite previous tariffs increasing costs for manufacturers, car dealerships have absorbed the "lion's share" to date, according to Bernard Yaros, lead economist at Oxford Economics.

"But that cushion is wearing thin," he adds. "The recently threatened 50% tariffs on Canadian autos, trucks, and car parts would feed through to consumer prices more readily than before."

Yaros thinks higher costs on imports to the US could accelerate a trend of manufacturers prioritising luxury cards, SUVs and pick-up trucks and push up prices in the used-car market if supplies of new but less-expensive vehicles becomes tight.

Carney has decided not to match Trump's 50% tariff threat so far, but a 25% import tax on certain American vehicles has been in place since last year.

Construction materials such as steel, aluminium as well as lumber wood have had tariffs in place before the latest escalation, though Canada has now matched US rates on the metals at 50%.

Carney has also imposed import taxes on several US wood products, such as plywood, and even screws used to fix timber together.

That means building firms that import such materials will face higher costs and may choose to pass those on through higher prices - pushing up the cost of homes, for example.

The Forest Products Association of Canada says tariffs would "raise costs on both sides of the border", while on the US side, Bill Owens, chairman of the National Association of Home Builders (NAHB) urged Trump to make building materials exempt from his tariff agenda due to an "ongoing housing affordability crisis".

"Building material tariffs heighten market uncertainty, strain supply chains and increase construction costs," he says.

In 2024 the US imported $23bn (C$32bn, £17bn) worth of wood products, with almost half from Canada, according to a US Congress report.

body.zh: 在美国和加拿大之间的贸易战最近升级期间，宣布了一系列新关税。 自美国总统唐纳德·特朗普重返白宫后推出其旗舰贸易政策以来，北美邻国一直陷入激烈的经济冲突。 本周，加拿大采取了最新举措，在特朗普威胁要加税后，加拿大总理马克·卡尼对大量美国商品征收报复性进口税。 随着这场针锋相对的关税争端尘埃落定，边境双方受影响最大的是什么？ 如果特朗普威胁从2027年1月1日起将加拿大汽车关税从25%提高到50%成为现实，那么这将对汽车行业造成进一步打击。 汽车、卡车和零部件是美国、加拿大和墨西哥之间的主要贸易商品，制造业和供应链跨越国界。 牛津经济研究院首席经济学家伯纳德·雅罗斯表示，尽管此前的关税增加了制造商的成本，但迄今为止汽车经销商已经吸收了“最大份额”。 “但是那个垫子已经变薄了，”他补充道。 “最近威胁对加拿大汽车、卡车和汽车零部件征收 50% 的关税将比以前更容易影响消费者价格。” 雅罗斯认为，美国进口成本上升可能会加速制造商优先生产豪华卡、SUV 和皮卡车的趋势，如果新型但价格较低的车辆供应紧张，则会推高二手车市场的价格。 到目前为止，卡尼已决定不响应特朗普的 50% 关税威胁，但自去年以来已对某些美国车辆征收 25% 的进口税。 在最近一次升级之前，钢铁、铝和木材等建筑材料已经征收关税，尽管加拿大现在对这些金属的关税达到了 50%，与美国相当。 卡尼还对几种美国木制品征收进口税，例如胶合板，甚至用于将木材固定在一起的螺钉。 这意味着进口此类材料的建筑公司将面临更高的成本，并可能选择通过更高的价格来转嫁这些成本，例如推高房屋成本。 加拿大林产品协会表示，关税将“增加边境两边的成本”，而在美国方面，全国住宅建筑商协会(NAHB)主席比尔·欧文斯敦促特朗普将建筑材料排除在关税议程之外，因为“持续的住房负担能力危机”。 “建筑材料关税加剧了市场不确定性，给供应链带来压力，并增加了建筑成本，”他表示。 根据美国国会报告，2024 年美国进口了价值 230 亿美元（320 亿加元，170 亿英镑）的木制品，其中近一半来自加拿大。 但所谓的“木材战争”......

title.en: US and Venezuela reach 'historic' oil deal, Trump says
title.zh: 特朗普称美国和委内瑞拉达成“历史性”石油协议

summary.en: The agreement would grant the US majority control of over 65 billion barrels of proven Venezuelan oil reserves, Trump said.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及对脆弱群体的怜悯。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
The US has reached a deal with Venezuela to control more than 65 billion barrels of its proven oil reserves, according to President Donald Trump.

"This Historic Transaction MORE THAN DOUBLES American Oil Reserves, greatly increases our Oil Supply, and will substantially lower Gas Prices for all Americans," Trump posted on social media.

After the US arrested Venezuela's then-President Nicolás Maduro earlier this year, Trump vowed to tap its reserves – the world's largest. More recently, he has been under pressure to bring gas prices down at home.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio called the deal "a huge win for both the American and Venezuelan people". Details have not been released.

"For the Venezuelan people, this deal will bring nearly $100 billion in private investment, support thousands of high-paying jobs, and drive the reconstruction of Venezuela's economy," Rubio said on social media.

In his post, Trump said Rubio and Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth had reached the agreement with Venezuela's interim president, Delcy Rodriguez, "through a partnership with private business".

He did not elaborate on the partnership or describe possible commitments and terms for the US in the deal, but he did say the agreement was reached "at no cost to the American Taxpayer".

On 3 January, Maduro and his wife, Cilia Flores, were seized in a military operation authorised by Trump.

In the hours after the raid, Trump said his administration would run Venezuela until a "safe, proper and judicious transition" could take place, adding that the US would indefinitely control the sale of the country's oil.

Venezuela has the largest proven oil reserves in the world - an estimated 303 billion barrels. However, production has plummeted from its peak in the late 1990s.

Trump has asked US oil firms to invest at least $100bn (£75bn) to restore the country's oil industry.

He has also claimed the rights to Venezuela's oil after alleging that the country had in the past "unilaterally seized and sold American oil, American assets and American platforms, costing us billions and billions of dollars".
body.zh: 美国总统唐纳德·特朗普表示，美国已与委内瑞拉达成协议，控制其已探明石油储量超过 650 亿桶。 特朗普在社交媒体上发帖称：“这一历史性交易使美国石油储备增加了一倍多，大大增加了我们的石油供应，并将大幅降低所有美国人的天然气价格。” 今年早些时候，美国逮捕了委内瑞拉时任总统尼古拉斯·马杜罗后，特朗普发誓要动用其全球最大的储备。最近，他面临着降低国内天然气价格的压力。 国务卿马可·卢比奥称该协议“对美国和委内瑞拉人民来说都是巨大的胜利”。细节尚未公布。 卢比奥在社交媒体上表示：“对于委内瑞拉人民来说，这项协议将带来近1000亿美元的私人投资，支持数千个高薪就业岗位，推动委内瑞拉经济重建。” 特朗普在帖子中表示，卢比奥和国防部长皮特·赫格斯“通过与私营企业的合作”与委内瑞拉临时总统德尔西·罗德里格斯达成了协议。 他没有详细说明合作伙伴关系，也没有描述美国在协议中可能做出的承诺和条款，但他确实表示，该协议的达成“美国纳税人没有付出任何代价”。 1 月 3 日，马杜罗和他的妻子西莉亚·弗洛雷斯在特朗普授权的一次军事行动中被抓获。 袭击发生后几个小时，特朗普表示，他的政府将管理委内瑞拉，直到实现“安全、适当和明智的过渡”，并补充说美国将无限期控制该国石油销售。 委内瑞拉拥有世界上最大的已探明石油储量——估计为 3030 亿桶。然而，产量已从 20 世纪 90 年代末的峰值大幅下降。 特朗普已要求美国石油公司投资至少 1000 亿美元（750 亿英镑）来恢复该国的石油工业。 他还声称拥有委内瑞拉石油的权利，声称该国过去“单方面扣押和出售美国石油、美国资产和美国平台，使美国损失数十亿美元”。

title.en: Canada poaches dozens of top US researchers for its universities
title.zh: 加拿大为其大学挖走数十名美国顶尖研究人员

summary.en: Lured by millions of new research funding from the Carney government, 48 US researchers in fields like climate and medicine will soon be moving north.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及智慧、知识与追求真理。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Canada is hiring dozens of researchers away from US universities, including top research institutions such as Harvard as its relationship with its neighbour continues to sour.

More than three-fourths of the 64 professors who are moving to Canada from around the world will come from the US. Under a new government programme, they'll receive funding from a pool of C$504m ($362m; £268m) for research in fields such as climate change and medicine.

US President Donald Trump's administration has accused universities of being dominated by left-wing ideology and diversity policies, and of failing to tackle alleged campus antisemitism.

The administration has also frozen federal research grants for many different institutions and groups that they have argued are wasteful , external . That uncertainty is helping lure researchers elsewhere.

Meanwhile, Canada is asserting itself more on the global stage while it pushes back against the US in their escalating trade war, which reached a major turning point over tariffs recently .

One climate researcher told the BBC he was relocating to Canada in part because his work in the US had become more difficult in recent years.

Seth Guikema, a climate resiliency researcher at the University of Michigan and one of the 48 US researchers relocating to Canada, said he decided to approach Canadian institutions last year in search of opportunities.

"The funding environment in the US for anything related to climate and resilience has become challenging," Guikema said. "I was looking for a good intellectual home where I could have practical impact."

Over the next eight years, Guikema said he would use C$8m to research tools for better preparing for natural hazards, like storms and wildfires, at the University of Western Ontario.

Canada's Industry Minister Melanie Joly said on Thursday the government was "very glad that these fantastic professors are coming".

Asked if the programme was poaching US talent and whether it could be viewed by the Trump administration as an escalation of the US-Canada trade war, she said on Thursday: "The US administration is taking its own decisions and we're taking ours."

Some of the researchers chosen for the programme, like Guikema, were born and raised in the US. Others are Canadians who worked abroad and are now returning home.

Peter Caravan, who worked for two decades as a biopharmaceutical researcher and professor at Massachusetts General Hospital and Harvard Medical School, appeared emotional at a Thursday news conference announcing the research appointments.

Caravan is researching how illnesses like cancers and chronic diseases can be better detected - work that will now be done out of the University of British Columbia in Vancouver.

title.en: Man, 41, dies after large sign falls at Christian festival in West Sussex
title.zh: 西萨塞克斯基督教节大型标牌掉落后，41岁男子死亡

summary.en: Six more people hospitalised after incident at Big Church festival near Steyning A 41-year-old man has died and at least six other people have been injured after a large sign fell at a Christian festival in West Sussex, police said. The man, from Eastbourne, East Sussex, was...
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及在压力下的忠信与属灵勇气。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
A 41-year-old man has died and at least six other people have been injured after a large sign fell at a Christian festival in West Sussex , police said.

The man, from Eastbourne, East Sussex, was pronounced dead at the scene after the incident at the Big Church festival near Steyning on Friday afternoon.

His next of kin have been told and are being supported by specialist officers, Sussex police said.

The force added that at least six other people have been taken to hospital for treatment. DCS Richard McDonagh said: “This is a tragic incident and our thoughts go out to the man’s family and friends at this incredibly difficult time.”

Anyone with any information or relevant video footage has been asked to contact police.

In a post on Instagram shortly after 5.30pm, organisers told attenders the show had been cancelled and all day visitors “must leave the site now”.

Organisers later said they had decided to cancel the rest of the festival, which had been scheduled to run until Sunday.

“We are devastated by the serious incident that took place at Big Church festival 2026 today, in which a sign fell, injuring at least seven people, one of whom tragically lost their life,” the festival said in an online statement.

“First and foremost, all of our thoughts are with those who have been affected, their families and friends, and everyone who witnessed what happened.

“Following today’s incident, we have made the decision to bring Big Church festival 2026 to a close.”

Officers remained at the scene on Friday night, and people were advised to avoid the area.

The incident has been reported to the Health and Safety Executive and local authority, Sussex police said.

McDonagh added: “I recognise the immense distress this will have caused people at the festival, and we are working with a number of partners as we seek to establish exactly what happened.

“We know there were thousands of people at the festival and we’re urging anyone with any information, or any relevant video footage, to please come forward.”
body.zh: 警方称，西萨塞克斯郡一个基督教节日期间，一块大标牌掉落，造成一名 41 岁男子死亡，至少六人受伤。 周五下午，该男子来自东萨塞克斯郡伊斯特本，在斯泰宁附近的大教堂节日发生事件后，被宣布当场死亡。 苏塞克斯警方表示，他的近亲已被告知并得到了专业官员的支持。 警方补充说，至少有六人已被送往医院接受治疗。 DCS 理查德·麦克唐纳 (Richard McDonagh) 表示：“这是一起悲惨事件，在这个极其困难的时刻，我们向该男子的家人和朋友表示慰问。” 任何有任何信息或相关视频片段的人都被要求与警方联系。 下午 5 点 30 分后不久，组织者在 Instagram 上发帖称，演出已被取消，全天参观者“必须立即离开现场”。 组织者后来表示，他们决定取消原定于周日举行的音乐节剩余活动。 该节日在一份在线声明中表示：“我们对今天 2026 年大教堂节发生的严重事件感到震惊，其中一块标牌掉落，造成至少七人受伤，其中一人不幸丧生。” “首先，我们所有的想法都与那些受到影响的人、他们的家人和朋友以及目睹所发生事件的每个人同在。 “在今天的事件发生后，我们决定结束 2026 年大教堂节。” 周五晚上，警察仍留在现场，并建议人们避开该地区。 苏塞克斯警方表示，该事件已报告给健康与安全执行局和地方当局。 麦克唐纳补充道：“我认识到这会给音乐节上的人们带来巨大的痛苦，我们正在与许多合作伙伴合作，力求查明到底发生了什么。 “我们知道有数千人参加了音乐节，我们敦促任何有任何信息或相关视频片段的人挺身而出。”

In response, the Australian government is deploying rapid response team members to Kathmandu to assist with the unfolding crisis.

title.en: Footage of Tibet floods isn't being shown in China - and we know little about victims there
title.zh: 中国没有播放西藏洪水的镜头——我们对那里的受害者知之甚少

summary.en: Some of the most dramatic footage from the deadly flash flooding is hidden from public view in China.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及对脆弱群体的怜悯。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
The dramatic footage was almost impossible to miss. A torrent of water tearing through Gyirong Port, one of the main border crossings between Nepal and Tibet, sweeping away all in its path as hundreds of people fled for their lives.

The scenes, captured by CCTV cameras, quickly spread on social media and onto screens around the world.

Only a single still-frame shot has been broadcast so far by the country's state-run flagship news bulletin.

It has also been difficult to find the video on China's heavily censored internet. It is just as hard to even find posts describing the flash flooding that has claimed hundreds of lives, with just as many still unaccounted for since Wednesday.

Beijing has launched a massive rescue operation involving hundreds of emergency workers, which is continuing, and President Xi Jinping chaired an emergency meeting with officials to co-ordinate efforts.

But when you compare the country's internet content to what much of the world has been seeing online these past few days, China's firewall becomes more visible than ever.

Tibet, which Beijing annexed in the 1950s, had long resisted rule by the Chinese Communist Party.

China has quashed protests over the years, sometimes violently, and has been accused of grave rights violations in the Buddhist region. It has labelled the exiled spiritual leader, the Dalai Lama, a separatist.

That history means the very name Tibet draws China's censors. Beijing's sensitivities are especially apparent at times likes this.

There have been daily updates on the missing and the dead, and Beijing has also been posting updates on the rescue operations, as well as the dangers posed by a barrier lake that has been at risk of overflowing.

But there is little detail beyond that. There are no accounts from survivors in Tibet, and almost no user-generated footage showing the deadly moments or their aftermath.

We are yet to hear from anxious families of those missing. Trying to contact people there is near-impossible during regular times.

As a journalist who has covered North Korea, it has often been easier for me to contact interviewees in Pyongyang than it is in the Tibetan capital, Lhasa.

On Thursday night, as global headlines led on the devastation in a Himalayan valley, China's state broadcaster opened its main bulletin with the launch of Xi's new book, a selection of his "most important and fundamental works".

Foreign journalists cannot travel to Tibet without government permission. We have just a few hours to get as much information as we can on huge stories like this before videos are scrubbed and voices stifled.

Instead, we have to rely on state media, which has so far focused on incredibly dramatic rescue efforts.

Specialist search teams scaling mountains and cliff faces, or...
body.zh: 戏剧性的镜头几乎不可能被错过。尼泊尔和西藏之间的主要边境口岸之一吉隆口岸发生洪流，洪水冲垮了沿途的一切，数百人逃命。 这些场景被闭路电视摄像机捕捉到，迅速在社交媒体和世界各地的屏幕上传播。 到目前为止，该国官方旗舰新闻公报只播放了一个静态画面。 在中国严格审查的互联网上也很难找到这段视频。同样很难找到描述这场夺去了数百人生命的山洪的帖子，自周三以来仍有同样多的人下落不明。 北京已启动了涉及数百名应急人员的大规模救援行动，该行动仍在继续，国家主席习近平主持召开了官员紧急会议，协调救援行动。 但当你将中国的互联网内容与过去几天世界上大部分地区在网上看到的内容进行比较时，中国的防火墙变得比以往任何时候都更加明显。 北京在 20 世纪 50 年代吞并的西藏长期以来一直反抗中国共产党的统治。 多年来，中国镇压了抗议活动，有时甚至是暴力镇压，并被指控在佛教地区严重侵犯人权。它给流亡精神领袖达赖喇嘛贴上了分离主义者的标签。 这段历史意味着中国审查机构用“西藏”这个名字来命名。北京的敏感性在这种时候尤其明显。 每天都有关于失踪和死亡的最新消息，北京也一直在发布救援行动的最新消息，以及堰塞湖面临溢出风险所带来的危险。 但除此之外就没有什么细节了。没有西藏幸存者的叙述，也几乎没有用户生成的视频显示致命时刻或后果。 我们还没有收到失踪者焦急的家人的消息。平时想要联系那里的人几乎是不可能的。 作为一名报道朝鲜的记者，我在平壤联系受访者往往比在西藏首府拉萨更容易。 周四晚上，当全球头条新闻报道喜马拉雅山谷的灾难时，中国国家广播公司以习近平新书的发布作为其主要公报的开篇，该书精选了他的“最重要和最基础的著作”。 未经政府许可，外国记者不得前往西藏。在视频被删除、声音被压制之前，我们只有几个小时的时间来尽可能多地获取有关此类重大事件的信息。 相反，我们必须依靠官方媒体，迄今为止，官方媒体一直专注于令人难以置信的戏剧性救援工作。 专业搜索队攀登山脉和悬崖，或者……

title.en: Number of Australians missing in Nepal-Tibet floods rises amid warning of looming crisis
title.zh: 危机迫在眉睫，尼泊尔和西藏洪水中失踪的澳大利亚人人数增加

summary.en: Rescuers are searching for more than 2,400 missing people, with Australians joining the hunt for loved ones.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及对脆弱群体的怜悯。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Aid organisations are warning of a looming humanitarian disaster as the death toll continues to rise from catastrophic floods in Nepal and Tibet.

On Friday, the number of people missing in Nepal more than doubled to above 2,400, including 41 Australians, after a landslide of ice and rock burst the banks of the Trishuli River on Wednesday. At least 580 people were killed.

Chinese and Nepalese authorities have warned further flooding may occur, complicating rescue efforts and posing a risk to communities in the area.

The number of Australians confirmed missing rose to 41 on Saturday, but on Friday, one person made contact with their family.

Several Australians with family in the affected region have flown to assist the search for survivors, combing towns impacted by debris and torrents of mud.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

Among them is the husband of NSW mother-of-two Reshma Patel, who was due to touch down in Kathmandu on Friday evening.

Her last known location was an immigration office along the Nepal-Tibet border, which was captured in viral footage that showed it inundated with floodwaters.

"She was inside the big building, which you can see in all the videos that had been hit hard by the floods at the border," family friend Chin Valsan told AAP.

Patel had been travelling with the Isha Foundation for almost two weeks, and was due to catch a flight home to Sydney from Kathmandu on Thursday.

While search-and-rescue operations, aided by Australian officials, are ongoing, charities have banded together to launch a national aid appeal.

The Nepal Flood Disaster Appeal was established by a coalition of 15 Australian charities including Oxfam Australia and Save the Children Australia.

The group, known as the Emergency Action Alliance, has warned survivors may find themselves cut off from reliable shelter, food, drinking water and medical care.

It is a fear shared by Kiran Thapa, 46, who told AAP his family in Nepal had survived the floods, but the real "trauma" would come once the dust had settled.

The paddy fields his family relies on for food had been destroyed while he worried his elderly mother may not have access to medication for weeks.

"After a few weeks or so, when they come to the realisation that they've lost everything ... that may be very hard for them to digest," he said.

Foreign Minister Penny Wong unveiled a $5 million assistance package for communities affected by the floods, including $1 million to the Emergency Action Alliance.

The Australian Red Cross has announced all donations to its global emergency fund from Thursday would go to Nepal, while World Vision Australia has launched its own dedicated appeal.

title.en: Berlin is being blackmailed by hackers, mayor says
title.zh: 市长称柏林正遭受黑客勒索

summary.en: Kai Wegner says the German capital and city-state would not cave in to a ransom demand for data stolen in a cyber-attack.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Berlin is being blackmailed by hackers who were able to compromise city systems and steal data earlier this month, its mayor has said.

Kai Wegner said officials would not cave in to the ransom demand, which came on Thursday evening. He did not say how much was being sought, though Der Spiegel reports the hackers are demanding 30 bitcoin, worth around €2m (£1.7m).

Some of the German capital's online systems were forced to close down as a result of the attack, while investigators were working to understand what data had been taken.

The Rhysida group, which is thought to operate from Russia and eastern Europe, and was behind a previous attack on the British Museum, has reportedly taken responsibility.

It has said on its website it intends to begin auctioning the 5.79 terabytes of data it was able to steal from Berlin in seven days' time, according to news agency Reuters.

He said state police, prosecutors and federal security services were working to investigate the suspected perpetrators "with the utmost urgency", adding that inquiries into the "content and scope of the compromised data are being pursued with great intensity".

Officials for the city-state said an initial data leak occurred between 7 and 12 August.

Then, on 14 August, two department networks were shut down, making applications for housing benefits and payments impossible for several days.

Forensic investigations had since revealed further data leaks within Berlin's transport and environment department, officials said.

"It cannot be ruled out that personal or other non-public data may also be affected," the mayor's office said in a statement on Friday.

Authorities in the capital have not named the suspected cyber-attackers, though Der Spiegel is carrying a screenshot of the Rhysida group's dark web site claiming to possess files including contracts, non-disclosure agreements, personnel files, passwords and thousands of personal contact details.

It is also displaying a countdown, after which it says it will begin auctioning off the data with a starting price of 30 bitcoin - the same amount of the cryptocurrency being sought from Berlin, the German newspaper reports.

The Rhysida group has claimed hundreds of attacks since it emerged in 2023, studies say, and the group has targeted government insititutions and businesses of varying sizes in numerous countries.

It successfully infiltrated the British Museum's computer systems in 2023, disrupting services and stealing around 500,000 files.

When the UK institution refused to pay the ransom, the group published the files - containing the personal data of visitors, subscribers and staff - on the dark web.

body.zh: 柏林市长表示，本月早些时候，柏林正遭受黑客勒索，这些黑客能够破坏城市系统并窃取数据。 凯·韦格纳表示，官员们不会屈服于周四晚上提出的赎金要求。尽管《明镜周刊》报道称，黑客索要 30 个比特币，价值约 200 万欧元（170 万英镑），但他没有透露索要多少钱。 德国首都的一些在线系统因袭击而被迫关闭，而调查人员正在努力了解哪些数据被窃取。 Rhysida 组织据信在俄罗斯和东欧开展活动，是之前大英博物馆袭击事件的幕后黑手，据报道，该组织已承担责任。 据路透社报道，该公司在其网站上表示，打算开始拍卖 7 天内从柏林窃取的 5.79 TB 数据。 他表示，州警察、检察官和联邦安全部门正在“极其紧急”地调查涉嫌肇事者，并补充说，正在大力调查“受损数据的内容和范围”。 这个城邦国家的官员表示，最初的数据泄露发生在 8 月 7 日至 12 日期间。 然后，8 月 14 日，两个部门网络被关闭，导致数天内无法申请住房福利和付款。 官员们表示，法证调查显示柏林交通和环境部门内部存在进一步的数据泄露事件。 市长办公室在周五的一份声明中表示：“不能排除个人或其他非公开数据也可能受到影响。” 首都当局尚未透露可疑网络攻击者的名字，但《明镜周刊》刊登了 Rhysida 组织暗网的屏幕截图，声称拥有合同、保密协议、人事档案、密码和数千个个人联系方式等文件。 据德国报纸报道，该公司还显示了倒计时，之后表示将开始以 30 比特币的起始价格拍卖这些数据，这与从柏林寻求的加密货币数量相同。 研究称，自 2023 年出现以来，Rhysida 组织已发起了数百起攻击，该组织的目标是多个国家不同规模的政府机构和企业。 它于 2023 年成功渗透大英博物馆的计算机系统，中断服务并窃取约 500,000 个文件。 当英国机构拒绝支付赎金时，该组织在暗网上发布了包含访问者、订阅者和工作人员个人数据的文件。 柏林网络攻击发生在该市举行选举前大约一个月，尽管州参议员艾里斯·斯普兰格坚称……

title.en: What next? Kurds say yes, Druze still say no to united Syria
title.zh: 接下来怎么办？库尔德人说是，德鲁兹仍然对统一叙利亚说不

summary.en: The Druze minority in Sweida, Syria, is now the only group that hasn't accepted central government authority. How does the end of an independent Kurdish area impact Druze plans for a different, divided kind of Syria?
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及领导、智慧与公共责任。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
The Druze minority in Sweida, Syria, is now the only group that hasn't accepted central government authority. How does the end of an independent Kurdish area impact Druze plans for a different, divided kind of Syria?

This week, Syria's Kurdish minority agreed to dissolve what had been their almost 14-year-long experiment in independent rule.

During the Syrian civil war, which began in 2011, the Kurds consolidated their authority over a large part of northeastern Syria, and wanted to maintain that after the civil war ended. But as Kurdish leader Mazloum Abdi said this week, "circumstances have changed."

Kurdish fighting forces, which go by the name of the Syrian Democratic Forces, or SDF, will now be integrated into the general Syrian military, and the oil-rich area they ruled will come under the authority of the central government.

All this means that Sweida province, home to much of Syria's Druze minority, is now the only area not to have accepted the authority of the central government.

There is no doubt that the change in the situation with Syria's Kurdish community will affect what is happening in Sweida, experts say.

When Omer Ozkizilcik, a nonresident senior fellow at US think tank, the Atlantic Council's Syria Project, met with Sheikh Hikmat al-Hijri in early 2025, the Druze leader said he was in daily phone contact with Abdi.

"He said that they were coordinating all their efforts and that they had a similar political vision for Syria — that is, decentralized with autonomous regions," said Ozkizilcik. "He basically repeated the Israeli approach, where they believe Syria should be divided, with an autonomous zone on the coast for the Alawite [minority], for the SDF in the northeast, and then in the south for the Druze. That shows that al-Hijiri's political vision was highly dependent on his alliance with the SDF."

That idea is no longer feasible. "Basically it puts an end to this vision of a fragmented, weak and decentralized Syria," the Ankara-based analyst argued.

That is also probably the reason why, earlier this week, al-Hijri again emphasized the Druze ties to Israel, Ozkizilcik suggested.

On Monday in Sweida, al-Hijiri declared the Druze an "inseparable part of the state of Israel."

​​​​​​But it's clear that having Israel annex Sweida would be very difficult for a number of reasons, including geography and demographics. Sweida is also still dependent on the central Syrian government. Despite it being impossible for government forces to enter the area, Sweida still receives public services, salaries, pensions, power and water from Damascus.

The exclusion of government forces began after intercommunal violence in Sweida in July 2025 . Fighting started between Druze and Bedouin locals. Government forces...
body.zh: 叙利亚苏维达的德鲁兹少数民族是目前唯一不接受中央政府权威的群体。独立库尔德地区的终结如何影响德鲁兹人建立一个不同的、分裂的叙利亚的计划？ 本周，叙利亚库尔德少数民族同意终止他们长达近 14 年的独立统治实验。 在 2011 年开始的叙利亚内战期间，库尔德人巩固了对叙利亚东北部大部分地区的权力，并希望在内战结束后维持这种权力。但正如库尔德领导人马兹鲁姆·阿卜迪本周所说，“情况已经发生了变化。” 名为“叙利亚民主力量”（SDF）的库尔德武装现在将并入叙利亚军队，他们统治的石油资源丰富的地区将置于中央政府的管辖之下。 所有这一切意味着，叙利亚德鲁兹少数民族大部分人居住的苏韦达省现在是唯一不接受中央政府权威的地区。 专家表示，毫无疑问，叙利亚库尔德社区局势的变化将影响苏韦达的局势。 2025 年初，当美国智囊团大西洋理事会叙利亚项目的非常驻高级研究员奥马尔·奥兹克兹吉克 (Omer Ozkizilcik) 会见谢赫·希克马特·希吉里 (Sheikh Hikmat al-Hijri) 时，这位德鲁兹领导人表示，他每天都与阿卜迪保持电话联系。 厄兹基济尔奇克说：“他说，他们正在协调所有努力，并且对叙利亚有类似的政治愿景，即通过自治区进行权力下放。” “他基本上重复了以色列的做法，他们认为叙利亚应该被划分，在沿海为阿拉维派（少数民族）建立一个自治区，在东北部为自卫队建立一个自治区，然后在南部为德鲁兹人建立一个自治区。这表明圣希里的政治愿景高度依赖于他与自卫队的联盟。” 这个想法已经不可行了。这位驻安卡拉的分析人士认为，“基本上，它结束了叙利亚支离破碎、虚弱和权力分散的愿景。” 厄兹克兹齐克表示，这也可能是本周早些时候阿尔希里再次强调德鲁兹派与以色列关系的原因。 周一，阿尔希吉里在苏维达宣布德鲁兹派是“以色列国不可分割的一部分”。 ​​​​​​但很明显，由于地理和人口等多种原因，让以色列吞并苏韦达将非常困难。苏维达还仍然依赖叙利亚中央政府。尽管政府军无法进入该地区，苏维达仍然从大马士革获得公共服务、工资、养老金、电力和水。 2025 年 7 月苏韦达发生部族间暴力事件后，政府军开始被排除在外。德鲁兹人和贝都因人当地人之间爆发了战斗。政府军...

title.en: Uganda: World's 'youngest monarch' dies aged 34
title.zh: 乌干达：世界上“最年轻的君主”去世，享年34岁

summary.en: Oyo Nyimba, once recognized as the world's youngest reigning monarch, has died in his mid-30s. As one of Uganda's traditional monarchs, he took the throne of the Tooro kingdom in 1995, aged just 3.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.zh: 奥约·宁巴（Oyo Nyimba）曾被认为是世界上最年轻的在位君主，现已去世，年仅 30 多岁。作为乌干达传统君主之一，他于1995年登上托罗王国王位，年仅3岁。 托罗总理周四晚间宣布，乌干达前殖民传统王国托罗的国王奥约·宁巴 (Oyo Nyimba) 去世，年仅 34 岁。 托罗地区领导人卡尔文·阿姆斯特朗·卢米埃尔·阿基基 (Calvin Armstrong Rwomiire Akiiki) 在社交媒体上表示：“我怀着深切的悲伤和沉重的心情宣布托罗的奥穆卡马国王奥约·宁巴·卡班巴·卡班巴·伊古鲁·鲁基迪四世去世。” 乌干达是一个共和国，由议会和名义上选举产生的国家元首、长期任职的总统约韦里·穆塞韦尼（Yoweri Museveni）统治，他自 1986 年以来一直执政。 但该国保留了几个传统的君主制，这些君主制仍然按照前殖民时期的方式统治着它们的王国。他们的权力在很大程度上是象征性的，但他们具有相当大的文化和社会影响力。 尽管 1962 年脱离英国殖民统治独立后，一位共和党总统表示他希望统一这个新生国家，从而禁止了传统君主制，但穆塞韦尼还是在 1993 年恢复了传统君主制。 奥约·宁巴 (Oyo Nyimba) 可以说是其中最知名的一个，尤其是因为他不寻常的故事，他于 1995 年年仅 3 岁就登上了王位。 地区领导人阿基基 (Akiiki) 表示，国王于周四晚些时候去世，但没有透露死因。他表示，稍后将发表一份包含葬礼和哀悼安排等更多细节的官方声明。 他呼吁托罗人民“在这个困难时期保持团结、冷静和祈祷”。 阿基基还对这位未婚的年轻国王发表了一项令人惊讶的说法，他从很小的时候起就被视为乌干达最有资格的单身汉。 “王室的连续性是有保证的，”他说。 “陛下留下一位王子作为继承人，他的身份将在适当的时候按照托罗王国的传统和习俗正式公布。” 奥约·宁巴（Oyo Nyimba）的去世引发了网上的悲痛和乌干达全国的广泛报道。 奥约出生于1992年4月16日，是已故奥姆卡马·帕特里克·大卫·马修·卡博约·奥利米三世和女王贝斯特·凯米吉萨·卡博约​​的第二个孩子，有两个姐妹。 1995年，他父亲去世后，他在乌干达西部靠近刚果边境的托罗地区继承了王位。 他作为现代“男孩国王”的不同寻常的地位在他统治初期引起了相当大的兴趣，包括多次访问托罗的前利比亚强人穆阿迈尔·卡扎菲等世界领导人。 奥约的母亲是他年轻时的重要顾问之一，总统约韦里也是如此……

title.en: Africa's aging autocrats fight to stay in power
title.zh: 非洲年迈的独裁者们为保住权力而战

summary.en: Some of Africa's longest-serving leaders are employing various tactics to extend their rule as they age, facing new challenges from succession battles and public pressure.
summary.zh: 随着年龄增长，非洲一些在位时间最长的领导人正采取不同策略以延长其统治，但年龄、继位之争和公众压力带来了新的挑战。

body.en:
As some of Africa's longest-serving leaders grow older, they are using different tactics to extend their rule. But age, succession battles and public pressure pose new challenges.

Power can be seductive, and many who possess it want to hold on for as long as possible. The leaders of China  and Russia , for example, cleared the way for additional terms years ago, and in the United States, the president occasionally speaks of another run for office, even though the US Constitution does not allow it.

From the perspective of Paul Biya, however, Chinese President  Xi Jinping , Russian President  Vladimir Putin and US President  Donald Trump are still relatively new to office.

Cameroon's president has been head of state since 1982. In 2025, Biya began his eighth term  — which is officially due to end on November 6, 2032, just a few months before his 100th birthday.

The 93-year-old has given no official indication that he intends to step down , and the position of vice president remains vacant.

During his 44 years in office, Biya has built a stable network of loyal allies that keeps the machinery of government running despite his lengthy absences.

The 93-year-old has now spent two and a half months in Geneva, Switzerland, continuing to issue decrees and make personnel decisions from abroad. In mid-June, his spokesperson denied rumors Biya was receiving treatment in a hospital and stated that the president was in good health.

"There is continuity, but that also means there is little momentum for reform within the government,” Beverly Ochieng, senior analyst at consultancy Global Risk, told DW.

And while Biya's power apparatus has helped cushion the impact of the president's long absence, that does not necessarily mean the most influential figures on the ground are united. After all, a post-Biya era is now in sight , and several of his allies are rumored to have ambitions of succeeding him.

"When everyone is lining up to potentially succeed Biya, it also means that the elites may begin challenging one another," Ochieng said. Such rivalry, she warned, could lead to major disruptions, including the possibility of a military coup.

Analyst Levi Mboushou recently voiced similar concerns on DW's AfricaLink podcast.

"Everyone feels the fear and uncertainty, but no one dares to look directly at it because we all have to deal with this repressive regime. You see something, but you say nothing. That is the situation in Cameroon  at the moment," he said.

Ugandan President Yoweri Museveni is only slightly younger, both in age and years in office.

The 81-year-old has been president since 1986 and, like Biya, recently embarked on another term . His succession also remains unresolved, although his son, Muhoozi...
body.zh: 随着非洲一些任职时间最长的领导人年龄的增长，他们正在使用不同的策略来延长他们的统治。但年龄、继承之争和公众压力带来了新的挑战。 权力是诱人的，许多拥有权力的人都想尽可能长时间地保留权力。例如，中国和俄罗斯领导人多年前就为追加任期扫清了道路，而在美国，总统偶尔会谈到再次竞选总统，尽管宪法不允许。 然而，从保罗·比亚的角度来看，中国国家主席习近平、俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京和美国总统唐纳德·特朗普仍相对较新上任。 喀麦隆总统自 1982 年起担任国家元首。2025 年，他开始了第八个任期，正式任期将于 2032 年 11 月 6 日结束，距他的 100 岁生日仅几个月。 这位93岁的老人没有正式表示他打算辞职，副总统职位仍然空缺。因此，比亚是今年采取进一步措施以确保掌权的几位非洲领导人之一。 在其 44 年的执政生涯中，比亚建立了一个稳定的忠诚盟友网络，尽管他长期缺席，但该网络仍使政府机构保持运转。 这位93岁的老人如今已经在瑞士日内瓦度过了两个半月的时间，继续在国外发布法令、做出人事决定。 6月中旬，其发言人否认了比亚正在医院接受治疗的传闻，并表示比亚身体状况良好。 咨询公司Global Risk的高级分析师贝弗利·奥钦(Beverly Ochieng)对德国之声表示：“存在连续性，但这也意味着政府内部改革动力不大。” 尽管比亚的权力机构帮助缓解了总统长期缺席的影响，但这并不一定意味着当地最有影响力的人物是团结的。毕竟，后比亚时代即将到来，据传他的几个盟友都有接替他的野心。 奥钦说：“当每个人都在排队等待比亚的接班人时，这也意味着精英们可能会开始相互挑战。”她警告说，这种竞争可能会导致重大混乱，包括发生军事政变的可能性。 分析师 Levi Mboushou 最近在德国之声的 Africalink 播客上表达了类似的担忧。 “每个人都感受到恐惧和不确定性，但没有人敢直视它，因为我们都必须应对这个高压政权。你看到了一些东西，但你什么也没说。这就是喀麦隆目前的情况。” 乌干达总统约韦里·穆塞韦尼无论是在年龄还是在任年限上都只稍微年轻一些。 这位 81 岁的老人自 1986 年以来一直担任总统，和比亚一样，最近......

title.en: Serbia: Keeping EU, Russia in play ahead of key election
title.zh: 塞尔维亚：在关键选举前让欧盟和俄罗斯参与其中

summary.en: As Serbia heads towards an uncertain election, President Aleksandar Vucic is balancing ties with Russia and EU ambitions. But growing geopolitical tensions and pressure at home are narrowing his room to maneuver.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及领导、智慧与公共责任。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
As Serbia heads towards an uncertain election, President Aleksandar Vucic is balancing ties with Russia and EU ambitions. But growing geopolitical tensions and pressure at home are narrowing his room to maneuver.

Smoke from the wildfires still hangs over parts of Serbia , but as the flames slowly recede, another debate is taking shape in their wake — one that has less to do with firefighting and more with politics.

In early August, wildfires swept across Serbia, affecting more than 3,500 hectares (8,600 acres) in the Deliblato Sands Special Nature Reserve alone. For days, firefighters, soldiers and helicopters battled the flames.

Then a Russian Ilyushin Il-76 firefighting aircraft arrived in the southern city of Nis. Serbia had turned to Moscow for help, making Russia the first foreign country it asked to provide a firefighting aircraft. Pro-government media greeted its arrival with celebratory coverage, dubbing the aircraft the "Russian beast."

"Considering that there are no firefighting aircraft of this capacity available within the European Union , the arriving Russian aircraft will significantly strengthen our capacities to fight the fires," said Luka Causic, head of the Serbian Interior Ministry's Department for Emergency Situations.

The episode, however, was already being viewed through a geopolitical lens, as Serbia had sought Russian assistance before activating the EU's emergency mechanism.

When it did, the response was swift. Brussels mobilized four helicopters from its strategic rescEU reserve , based in Czechia, Romania and Slovakia, along with ground firefighting teams from Germany and Romania.

Vucic rejected the idea that turning to Russia first was a foreign-policy decision or a sign of Serbia's political alignment with Moscow.

"As far as equipment and resources are concerned, we are a European giant. The helicopters we received from Europe to fight the fires are less capable than ours and have a lower carrying capacity than our own," Vucic said during a visit to the Deliblato Sands.

The wildfire episode came less than two weeks after Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy made his first official visit to Serbia.

The two presidents reaffirmed their support for each other's territorial integrity, which is particularly significant for Belgrade because Ukraine does not recognise Kosovo's independence.

But Vucic is also trying to keep the other side on board, says Vuk Vuksanovic , a political scientist and foreign-policy lecturer at King's College London.

Vuksanovic argues that Vucic's engagement with Zelenskyy must therefore be portrayed in Moscow not as a fundamental shift in Serbia's relationship with Russia, but as a response to Western pressure and Serbia's own interests.

body.zh: 随着塞尔维亚大选走向不确定，总统亚历山大·武契奇正在平衡与俄罗斯和欧盟野心的关系。但日益加剧的地缘政治紧张局势和国内压力正在缩小他的回旋余地。 野火产生的烟雾仍然笼罩在塞尔维亚部分地区，但随着火焰慢慢消退，另一场辩论正在形成——这场辩论与消防无关，更多与政治有关。 8 月初，野火席卷了塞尔维亚，仅德利布拉托金沙特别自然保护区就影响了超过 3,500 公顷（8,600 英亩）的土地。连日来，消防员、士兵和直升机一直在与大火搏斗。 随后一架俄罗斯伊尔76型消防机抵达南部城市尼什。塞尔维亚向莫斯科寻求帮助，使俄罗斯成为第一个请求提供消防飞机的国家。亲政府媒体以庆祝性报道欢迎这架飞机的到来，称这架飞机为“俄罗斯野兽”。 塞尔维亚内政部紧急情况司司长卢卡·考西克表示：“考虑到欧盟境内没有具备这种能力的消防飞机，抵达的俄罗斯飞机将大大增强我们的灭火能力。” 然而，这一事件已经被从地缘政治的角度看待，因为塞尔维亚在启动欧盟紧急机制之前曾寻求俄罗斯的援助。 当它发生时，反应很快。布鲁塞尔从其驻捷克、罗马尼亚和斯洛伐克的战略救援储备中调动了四架直升机，以及来自德国和罗马尼亚的地面消防队。 武契奇否认首先转向俄罗斯是一项外交政策决定或塞尔维亚与莫斯科政治结盟的标志。 “就设备和资源而言，我们是欧洲巨头。我们从欧洲接收的用于灭火的直升机的能力不如我们的，运载能力也低于我们自己的，”武契奇在参观德利布拉托金沙时说道。 这场山火发生在乌克兰总统泽连斯基首次正式访问塞尔维亚后不到两周。 两国总统重申支持彼此的领土完整，这对贝尔格莱德尤为重要，因为乌克兰不承认科索沃独立。 但伦敦国王学院政治学家兼外交政策讲师武克·武克萨诺维奇 (Vuk Vuksanovic) 表示，武契奇也在努力让对方参与其中。 武克萨诺维奇认为，因此莫斯科必须将武契奇与泽连斯基的接触描述为塞尔维亚与俄罗斯关系的根本转变，而不是对西方压力和塞尔维亚自身利益的回应。 “武契奇现在...

title.en: Australian woman feared missing in Nepal flood makes contact as disaster worsens
title.zh: 澳大利亚妇女担心在尼泊尔洪水中失踪，随着灾难的恶化，她与人取得了联系

summary.en: An Australian woman caught up in deadly flooding in Nepal has made contact with family.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及对脆弱群体的怜悯。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Australian authorities are urgently trying to reach a woman who made contact with family after surviving catastrophic flooding on the Nepal-China border.

The Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT) is engaging with local authorities on plans to assist the woman, who is understood to have been last reported in a remote area several days' hike from Kathmandu.

At least 38 Australians remain missing after an ice avalanche on Wednesday triggered Nepal's worst natural disaster in more than a decade.

Heavy continued rainfall is making rescue conditions difficult and unpredictable.

Further severe flooding, landslides and debris flows are predicted in the affected areas of Nepal and Tibet while a lake formed by the landslide has started to overflow.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

At least 538 people have died, Nepalese authorities said, while almost 1,000 remain missing.

Australian woman Sumi Adhikari was on a pilgrimage on the China-Nepal border when the catastrophic flash flooding hit.

Her husband Kailash Mansowar, who has not heard from her since, has travelled to the region from Sydney to find her, guided only by her iPhone's last location.

"I am here in Nepal now (since) yesterday and working with local authorities to find further information," he told the Australian Associated Press (AAP) on Friday.

Like many missing Australians, Adhikari was undertaking a group tour, in her case with the Isha Foundation.

She left Kathmandu on 14 August after flying from Sydney to trek to a sacred site near Tibet's Mount Kailash.

"Even the smallest piece of information could help bring her home," a widely shared post on social media announcing her disappearance reads.

A separate group of 15 Australians, including two boys aged 11 and 14, were travelling with US-based tourism operator Himalayan Glacier Adventure and Travel Company.

Sydney doctor Manoj Dharmaratnam, who was invited to join the sacred pilgrimage but chose not to go, prescribed several of his friends altitude medication and conducted injury assessments before they left Australia.

"One of them had an injury and I did tell her, maybe you're not fit to go on this trek," Dr Dharmaratnam told AAP.

"She actually called up and cancelled her trip ... but then she said I've bought the ticket, so I might as well go."

The Himalayan Glacier group included a well-respected Sydney couple with two sons in their 20s, both studying medicine in NSW, he said.

At least four Australians were travelling separately to tour groups, Foreign Minister Penny Wong said on Friday.

title.en: Norway's King Harald V, a unifying force who weathered family storms, dies at 89
title.zh: 挪威国王哈拉尔五世去世，享年 89 岁，他是经历家庭风暴的团结力量

summary.en: King Harald V of Norway remained a unifying figure in his country until the very end.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Norway's King Harald, a reformer who emerged from the shadow of his well-loved, extrovert father and spent more than three decades on the throne, died on Friday at the age of 89, the royal palace said, at a time of multiple crises for the Norwegian royal family.

"King Harald passed away peacefully at Oslo University Hospital on Friday 28 August," the royal palace said on its website.

Harald, who was Europe's oldest living monarch, was taken to hospital on 17 August. The palace said doctors were treating him for a bacterial infection in his blood.

In 2024, he had been hospitalised for an infection while on holiday in Malaysia and received a temporary pacemaker at a hospital there. The Norwegian armed forces flew him back home, and he was later fitted with a permanent device.

That same year, Harald, Norway's ceremonial head of state since 1991, said he would reduce the number of official engagements he took part in but ruled out abdication, insisting that his oath as king was for life.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

Crown Princess Mette-Marit, married to Harald's son Crown Prince Haakon, is facing intense scrutiny for her friendship with the late sex offender Jeffrey Epstein, a relationship for which she has apologised.

Her son Marius Hoiby, born from a relationship predating her marriage to Haakon, was found guilty in June of two out of four counts of rape and one count of domestic violence and sentenced to four years in prison after a seven-week trial. Both he and the prosecution have appealed the sentence.

Two days after Marius was convicted, the palace said Mette-Marit had undergone a successful lung transplant, without specifying when the procedure took place.

After several weeks of recovery in hospital, she returned home and celebrated her silver wedding anniversary with Haakon in August.

Support for the monarchy dropped to 60 per cent in February 2026, from 70 per cent the previous month, according to a Norstat poll published by state broadcaster NRK, rising slightly to 64 per cent in May.

Harald has remained consistently popular with Norwegians. According to the February poll, he was the royal who best represented the Norwegian royal family, with a score of 9.2, on a scale of one to 10.

A great-great-grandchild of Britain's Queen Victoria, Harald acceded to the throne in 1991 and gradually introduced modern touches that brought a ceremonial post, seen mainly as a symbol of national independence, into the 21st century.

The popular king played a crucial role in comforting the nation in times of mourning.

title.en: How Australians can help those impacted by devastating Nepal floods
title.zh: 澳大利亚人如何帮助受尼泊尔毁灭性洪水影响的人们

summary.en: Australian charities have launched a joint appeal to aid communities devastated by floods and landslides along the Nepal-China border. Thousands are in urgent need of shelter, food, clean water, and medical care after their homes and infrastructure were destroyed.
summary.zh: 澳大利亚慈善机构已发起联合募捐，以援助尼泊尔-中国边境受洪水和山体滑坡摧毁的社区。在房屋和基础设施被毁后，成千上万的人迫切需要住所、食物、清洁饮用水和医疗援助。

body.en:
Entire communities have been devastated by severe flooding and landslides along the Nepal-Tibet border, with homes, roads, bridges and critical infrastructure destroyed.

Search and rescue operations remain underway, while thousands of people are in urgent need of shelter, food, clean drinking water and medical assistance.

In response, 14 Australian charities have joined forces to launch a national appeal.

The Emergency Action Alliance (EAA) has launched the Nepal Flood Disaster Appeal, bringing together a variety of charities to support communities affected by the disaster.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

The alliance says donations will help provide immediate humanitarian assistance, including emergency shelter, food, safe drinking water, hygiene supplies and medical care.

Access to some affected communities remains difficult, with damaged roads and ongoing weather conditions hampering efforts to reach people in need.

Australians are encouraged to donate through the EAA website or by calling 1300 939 000.

The charities participating in the appeal are Save the Children Australia, Plan International Australia, Oxfam Australia, Australia for UNHCR, ActionAid Australia, CARE Australia, Caritas Australia, ADRA, Act for Peace, Anglican Overseas Aid, Australian Lutheran World Service, Baptist World Aid Australia, CBM Australia and Tearfund Australia.

EAA executive director Kerren Morris said the appeal provided Australians with a trusted way to support people affected by the disaster.

"Emergency shelter, food, safe drinking water and medical support are urgently needed now, while longer-term recovery efforts will continue for many months," she said in a statement.

The charities involved bring different areas of humanitarian expertise to the response, with organisations and their local partners working to provide immediate assistance to affected communities.

Save the Children is focusing on supporting children and families affected by humanitarian emergencies.

Oxfam Australia's humanitarian work includes support for essential services such as clean water, sanitation and emergency assistance.

Australia for UNHCR is the UN refugee agency's national partner in Australia, and is supporting humanitarian assistance through the UNHCR network.

The charities involved are continuing to assess the scale of the disaster and humanitarian needs in affected communities.

The EAA says its members are working to determine where support is most urgently needed as search and rescue operations continue.

title.en: Footage of Tibet floods isn't being shown in China - and we know little about victims there
title.zh: 中国没有播放西藏洪水的镜头——我们对那里的受害者知之甚少

summary.en: Some of the most dramatic footage from the deadly flash flooding is hidden from public view in China.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自中国栏目的新闻，重点涉及对脆弱群体的怜悯。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
The dramatic footage was almost impossible to miss. A torrent of water tearing through Gyirong Port, one of the main border crossings between Nepal and Tibet, sweeping away all in its path as hundreds of people fled for their lives.

The scenes, captured by CCTV cameras, quickly spread on social media and onto screens around the world.

Only a single still-frame shot has been broadcast so far by the country's state-run flagship news bulletin.

It has also been difficult to find the video on China's heavily censored internet. It is just as hard to even find posts describing the flash flooding that has claimed hundreds of lives, with just as many still unaccounted for since Wednesday.

Beijing has launched a massive rescue operation involving hundreds of emergency workers, which is continuing, and President Xi Jinping chaired an emergency meeting with officials to co-ordinate efforts.

But when you compare the country's internet content to what much of the world has been seeing online these past few days, China's firewall becomes more visible than ever.

Tibet, which Beijing annexed in the 1950s, had long resisted rule by the Chinese Communist Party.

China has quashed protests over the years, sometimes violently, and has been accused of grave rights violations in the Buddhist region. It has labelled the exiled spiritual leader, the Dalai Lama, a separatist.

That history means the very name Tibet draws China's censors. Beijing's sensitivities are especially apparent at times likes this.

There have been daily updates on the missing and the dead, and Beijing has also been posting updates on the rescue operations, as well as the dangers posed by a barrier lake that has been at risk of overflowing.

But there is little detail beyond that. There are no accounts from survivors in Tibet, and almost no user-generated footage showing the deadly moments or their aftermath.

We are yet to hear from anxious families of those missing. Trying to contact people there is near-impossible during regular times.

As a journalist who has covered North Korea, it has often been easier for me to contact interviewees in Pyongyang than it is in the Tibetan capital, Lhasa.

On Thursday night, as global headlines led on the devastation in a Himalayan valley, China's state broadcaster opened its main bulletin with the launch of Xi's new book, a selection of his "most important and fundamental works".

Foreign journalists cannot travel to Tibet without government permission. We have just a few hours to get as much information as we can on huge stories like this before videos are scrubbed and voices stifled.

Instead, we have to rely on state media, which has so far focused on incredibly dramatic rescue efforts.

Specialist search teams scaling mountains and cliff faces, or...
body.zh: 戏剧性的镜头几乎不可能被错过。尼泊尔和西藏之间的主要边境口岸之一吉隆口岸发生洪流，洪水冲垮了沿途的一切，数百人逃命。 这些场景被闭路电视摄像机捕捉到，迅速在社交媒体和世界各地的屏幕上传播。 到目前为止，该国官方旗舰新闻公报只播放了一个静态画面。 在中国严格审查的互联网上也很难找到这段视频。同样很难找到描述这场夺去了数百人生命的山洪的帖子，自周三以来仍有同样多的人下落不明。 北京已启动了涉及数百名应急人员的大规模救援行动，该行动仍在继续，国家主席习近平主持召开了官员紧急会议，协调救援行动。 但当你将中国的互联网内容与过去几天世界上大部分地区在网上看到的内容进行比较时，中国的防火墙变得比以往任何时候都更加明显。 北京在 20 世纪 50 年代吞并的西藏长期以来一直反抗中国共产党的统治。 多年来，中国镇压了抗议活动，有时甚至是暴力镇压，并被指控在佛教地区严重侵犯人权。它给流亡精神领袖达赖喇嘛贴上了分离主义者的标签。 这段历史意味着中国审查机构用“西藏”这个名字来命名。北京的敏感性在这种时候尤其明显。 每天都有关于失踪和死亡的最新消息，北京也一直在发布救援行动的最新消息，以及堰塞湖面临溢出风险所带来的危险。 但除此之外就没有什么细节了。没有西藏幸存者的叙述，也几乎没有用户生成的视频显示致命时刻或后果。 我们还没有收到失踪者焦急的家人的消息。平时想要联系那里的人几乎是不可能的。 作为一名报道朝鲜的记者，我在平壤联系受访者往往比在西藏首府拉萨更容易。 周四晚上，当全球头条新闻报道喜马拉雅山谷的灾难时，中国国家广播公司以习近平新书的发布作为其主要公报的开篇，该书精选了他的“最重要和最基础的著作”。 未经政府许可，外国记者不得前往西藏。在视频被删除、声音被压制之前，我们只有几个小时的时间来尽可能多地获取有关此类重大事件的信息。 相反，我们必须依靠官方媒体，迄今为止，官方媒体一直专注于令人难以置信的戏剧性救援工作。 专业搜索队攀登山脉和悬崖，或者……

title.en: Number of Australians missing in Nepal-Tibet floods rises amid warning of looming crisis
title.zh: 危机迫在眉睫，尼泊尔和西藏洪水中失踪的澳大利亚人人数增加

summary.en: Rescuers are searching for more than 2,400 missing people, with Australians joining the hunt for loved ones.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自中国栏目的新闻，重点涉及对脆弱群体的怜悯。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Aid organisations are warning of a looming humanitarian disaster as the death toll continues to rise from catastrophic floods in Nepal and Tibet.

On Friday, the number of people missing in Nepal more than doubled to above 2,400, including 41 Australians, after a landslide of ice and rock burst the banks of the Trishuli River on Wednesday. At least 580 people were killed.

Chinese and Nepalese authorities have warned further flooding may occur, complicating rescue efforts and posing a risk to communities in the area.

The number of Australians confirmed missing rose to 41 on Saturday, but on Friday, one person made contact with their family.

Several Australians with family in the affected region have flown to assist the search for survivors, combing towns impacted by debris and torrents of mud.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

Among them is the husband of NSW mother-of-two Reshma Patel, who was due to touch down in Kathmandu on Friday evening.

Her last known location was an immigration office along the Nepal-Tibet border, which was captured in viral footage that showed it inundated with floodwaters.

"She was inside the big building, which you can see in all the videos that had been hit hard by the floods at the border," family friend Chin Valsan told AAP.

Patel had been travelling with the Isha Foundation for almost two weeks, and was due to catch a flight home to Sydney from Kathmandu on Thursday.

While search-and-rescue operations, aided by Australian officials, are ongoing, charities have banded together to launch a national aid appeal.

The Nepal Flood Disaster Appeal was established by a coalition of 15 Australian charities including Oxfam Australia and Save the Children Australia.

The group, known as the Emergency Action Alliance, has warned survivors may find themselves cut off from reliable shelter, food, drinking water and medical care.

It is a fear shared by Kiran Thapa, 46, who told AAP his family in Nepal had survived the floods, but the real "trauma" would come once the dust had settled.

The paddy fields his family relies on for food had been destroyed while he worried his elderly mother may not have access to medication for weeks.

"After a few weeks or so, when they come to the realisation that they've lost everything ... that may be very hard for them to digest," he said.

Foreign Minister Penny Wong unveiled a $5 million assistance package for communities affected by the floods, including $1 million to the Emergency Action Alliance.

The Australian Red Cross has announced all donations to its global emergency fund from Thursday would go to Nepal, while World Vision Australia has launched its own dedicated appeal.

title.en: What we know about deadly Nepal-Tibet floods
title.zh: 关于造成数百人死亡的尼泊尔-西藏洪水的已知信息

summary.en: Hundreds have died or are missing in Wednesday's flooding and landslides on the border of Nepal and Tibet.
summary.zh: 周三，尼泊尔和西藏边境发生洪水和山体滑坡，造成数百人死亡或失踪。

body.en:
Devastating landslides and flash floods on the Nepal-Tibet border have caused widespread damage and left hundreds dead and thousands more missing.

At least 579 people have been killed and nearly 2,000 people remain unaccounted for, according to Nepal's National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority.

At least five people have died in Tibet, with another 558 reported missing by Chinese state media.

On Wednesday, flood water tore through the border region, sweeping away homes and roads, local officials have said.

Rescue workers say they now face a critical moment to reach remaining survivors as fears mount of further flooding in the disaster's aftermath.

Initial reports of an earthquake on the Nepal-Tibet border led many to believe that a tremor had caused a landslide, which in turn caused the devastating floods early on Wednesday.

However, the US Geological Survey (USGS) later confirmed that the disaster was caused by a "glacial collapse" - when a glacier or part of a glacier disintegrates.

The impact of the collapsed glacier hitting the bottom of a valley was so powerful that it registered a magnitude of 5.2, according to the agency, causing "subsequent catastrophic impacts downstream".

Powerful flood water and debris travelled some 62 miles (100km) downstream from the Trishuli and Bhote Koshi Rivers, the USGS said, sweeping through towns popular with mountaineering tourists and pilgrims in northern Nepal.

Footage showed a wall of mud and rock sweeping away buildings, roads and vehicles as people fled in the Nuwakot region.

In one video, a towering wall of water and mud was seen rushing down a gorge along the Trishuli River and enveloping the Rasuwagadhi Border checkpoint, a multi-storey building on the Nepalese side.

Gyirong Port, over the border, was also hit. A number of deaths were reported in Tibetan villages.

Scientists are trying to piece together the exact order of events as rescue efforts continue. Mike Searle, professor of Earth sciences at Oxford University, said the glacier could have collapsed "hours or days" before the flooding hit Nepal and Tibet.

"I think the sheer wave of debris suggests there was a landslide first, the water built up, [which] dammed the river, and then it burst in one huge great flood," he told the BBC.

The International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development (ICIDMOD) has warned secondary flooding could occur in the coming days as a result of debris that washed into the river systems.

The ICIDMOD said it was assessing whether the Trishuli River had been temporarily blocked in narrow sections. If this is the case, it is at risk of forming a landslide dam and a second flood.

Separately, China has warned there was a "high risk" a lake that formed after the landslide may burst its banks,...
body.zh: 尼泊尔和西藏边境发生的毁灭性山体滑坡和山洪造成大面积破坏，造成数百人死亡或失踪。 当地官员表示，洪水席卷边境地区，冲毁房屋和道路，两天以来，至少有 547 人死亡，977 人下落不明。 救援人员表示，他们现在面临着救助剩余幸存者的关键时刻，因为人们越来越担心灾难发生后会发生进一步的洪水。 尼泊尔和西藏边境发生地震的初步报道让许多人相信地震导致了山体滑坡，进而导致了周三早些时候的毁灭性洪水。 然而，美国地质调查局（USGS）后来证实，这场灾难是由“冰川崩塌”造成的，即冰川或冰川的一部分崩解。 据该机构称，崩塌的冰川撞击山谷底部的冲击力非常强大，达到了 5.2 级，“随后对下游造成了灾难性影响”。 美国地质勘探局表示，强大的洪水和碎片从特里苏里河和博特科希河下游流过约 62 英里（100 公里），席卷了尼泊尔北部深受登山游客和朝圣者欢迎的城镇。 视频显示，努瓦科特地区的人们纷纷逃离，泥石墙冲走了建筑物、道路和车辆。 在一段视频中，人们看到一堵高耸的水和泥墙沿着特里苏里河冲下峡谷，包围了拉苏瓦加迪边境检查站，这是尼泊尔一侧的一座多层建筑。 边境另一边的吉隆口岸也受到袭击。据报道，西藏村庄已有多人死亡。 随着救援工作的继续，科学家们正试图拼凑出事件的确切顺序。牛津大学地球科学教授迈克·塞尔表示，在洪水袭击尼泊尔和西藏之前“几小时或几天”，冰川可能已经崩塌。 他告诉英国广播公司：“我认为，巨大的碎片浪潮表明，首先发生了山体滑坡，水堆积起来，堵塞了河流，然后引发了一场巨大的洪水。” 国际山地综合开发中心（ICIDMOD）警告称，由于碎片冲入河流系统，未来几天可能会发生二次洪水。 ICIDMOD 表示正在评估 Trishuli 河的狭窄河段是否被暂时堵塞。如果真是这样，就有形成滑坡坝和二次洪水的危险。 另外，中国警告说，山体滑坡后形成的湖泊存在“高风险”，可能会决堤，导致下游出现新的洪水。据中央电视台报道，截至周五，估计已积水 250 万立方米。 官方媒体报道称，救援行动短暂...

reflection.en: The earth groans, Scripture tells us, in a kind of shared labor pain until now (Romans 8:22). This week's devastating floods and landslides on the Nepal-Tibet border, which have claimed hundreds of lives and left many more missing, are a stark reminder of that groaning. In the face of such immense loss, we are called to lament with those who grieve and to...
reflection.zh: 圣经告诉我们，直到如今，全创造一直藉着生产之苦同声唉哼（罗马书 8:22）。本周在尼泊尔-西藏边境发生的毁灭性洪水和山体滑坡，已夺走了数百人的生命，另有许多人失踪，这是对那呻吟的严峻提醒。面对如此巨大的损失，我们被呼召与哀恸者一同哀哭，并祈求全创造的更新。

title.en: Satellite images reveal scale of flood devastation in Nepal villages
title.zh: 卫星图像显示尼泊尔村庄遭受洪水破坏的规模

summary.en: Before-and-after images show villages, bridges and a key Nepal-Tibet border crossing washed away by devastating floodwaters.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自中国栏目的新闻，重点涉及对脆弱群体的怜悯。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
New satellite imagery has revealed the scale of the devastation along Nepal's Trishuli River caused by Wednesday's deadly flash flood, triggered by a glacier collapse.

Before-and-after images show how sections of the valley, where a torrent of floodwater and debris surged through, destroyed villages, bridges and hydroelectric power stations.

More than 550 people have been killed, Nepalese officials say, with hundreds more missing.

Among the worst-hit locations reviewed by BBC Verify was a key Nepal-Tibet border crossing, which was engulfed by a rush of floodwater and captured on camera.

The satellite imagery from US-based intelligence firm Vantor, shows the site has been almost entirely washed away. Shocking CCTV footage showed the moment as the deluge of water swept over buildings as people tried to escape.

Damage and mud can be seen more than 2.5km (1.5 miles) upstream, reaching 100m (330 ft) above the area it first hit.

A few miles further south is the village of Timure, which has now largely disappeared.

The walls of the valley at this point are steep, reaching up to 50m above the water line. The image shows most of the houses perched on this slope are now gone or covered in mud.

A further 10km (eight miles) downstream, where the Trishuli River winds through Syapru Besi, satellite imagery now shows the village covered by mud, rock and other debris. Houses and other structures have disappeared, including bridges and a hydroelectric power station.

One of the larger villages to be struck by the full force of the flood was Trishuli, where some of the earliest verified footage of the disaster emerged from.

A satellite image of the town and surrounding agricultural land, which is about 45km (28 miles) downstream from the border, show an entire neighbourhood has been essentially washed away.

Verified videos of the town show a bridge collapsing as the river surges forward. At the very same moment from ground level, footage filmed from inside a bus shows people crying out in distress and trying to flee as they see the water rushing down the river.

Other dramatic videos show people sheltering inside a house, peering over the edge of a balcony as they watch a torrent of floodwater wash away almost everything around them, knocking large metal debris and a vehicle toward the building.

Somehow the house remains intact and survivors can be seen in a second verified video standing surrounded by mud once the floodwater had receded.

Imagery from satellite provider Planet Labs released today has also provided a clearer view of the disaster's origins at the collapsed glacier, the moment of which has been captured on a verified drone video.

The satellite image shows an enormous chunk of the glacier has fallen away, carving an enormous path of rock and...
body.zh: 新的卫星图像揭示了周三冰川崩塌引发的致命山洪对尼泊尔特里苏利河沿岸造成的破坏规模。 前后照片显示了洪水和瓦砾汹涌而过的山谷部分地区如何摧毁了村庄、桥梁和水力发电站。 尼泊尔官员称，已有 550 多人丧生，数百人失踪。 BBC verify 审查的受灾最严重的地点之一是尼泊尔和西藏的一个重要过境点，该过境点被洪水淹没，并被摄像机拍摄到。 美国情报公司 Vantor 的卫星图像显示，该地点几乎完全被冲毁。令人震惊的闭路电视画面显示，当人们试图逃离时，洪水席卷建筑物。 在上游超过 2.5 公里（1.5 英里）处可以看到损坏和泥浆，到达其首次袭击区域上方 100 m（330 英尺）。 再往南几英里是蒂穆尔村，该村现已基本消失。 此时的山谷壁很陡，高出水线高达 50m。该图像显示，坐落在这个斜坡上的大多数房屋现在都已经消失或被泥土覆盖。 再往下游 10 公里（8 英里）处，Trishuli 河蜿蜒穿过 Syapru Besi，卫星图像现在显示该村庄被泥土、岩石和其他碎片覆盖。房屋和其他建筑物都消失了，包括桥梁和水力发电站。 Trishuli是遭受洪水全面袭击的较大村庄之一，一些最早经过核实的灾难镜头就来自那里。 该镇及周边农田（距离边境下游约 45 公里（28 英里））的卫星图像显示，整个社区基本上已被冲走。 经核实的该镇视频显示，随着河流汹涌澎湃，一座桥梁倒塌。就在同一时刻，从地面拍摄的公交车内拍摄的视频显示，人们看到河水顺流而下，痛苦地呼喊并试图逃跑。 其他戏剧性的视频显示，人们躲在房子里，从阳台边缘往外看，看到洪水冲走了他们周围的几乎所有东西，将大块金属碎片和一辆汽车冲向建筑物。 不知何故，房子仍然完好无损，在第二段经过验证的视频中可以看到洪水退去后幸存者被泥土包围。 卫星提供商 Planet Labs 今天发布的图像也提供了冰川崩塌灾难起源的更清晰视图，经过验证的无人机视频捕捉到了这一瞬间。 卫星图像显示，一大块冰川已经消失，形成了一条巨大的岩石路径……

title.en: Nepal-Tibet flood deaths pass 500, thousands still missing
title.zh: 尼泊尔和西藏洪水死亡人数超过500人，数千人仍失踪

summary.en: The Red Cross says more than 93,000 people are affected by the deadly floods and landslides on the China-Nepal border. Rescue efforts were temporarily paused after an overflowing lake threatened to trigger more floods.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自中国栏目的新闻，重点涉及对脆弱群体的怜悯。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
The Red Cross says more than 93,000 people are affected by the deadly floods and landslides on the China-Nepal border. Rescue efforts were temporarily paused after an overflowing lake threatened to trigger more floods.

Rescue workers have resumed a search for hundreds of people still missing two days after  catastrophic flash flooding  hit the border between  Nepal and  China . 

Their efforts were briefly put on hold on Friday after a lake formed by debris began overflowing, threatening areas already devastated by the disaster.  

"We have received a notice saying that the lake has broken its banks," Narendra Pariyar, the most senior bureaucrat of the hard-hit Rasuwa district, told DW. "We can see that the level of water in the river is rising."

Residents in Nepal's border district of Rasuwa were seen fleeing up hillsides as they braced for a surge in river levels, Reuters reported.

Authorities later said the threat had eased but that they were closely monitoring the situation. 

Meanwhile, Nepal said the death toll had risen to 579,  up from 390 a day earlier . China has updated its earlier count of three to five deaths in Tibet.

More than 2,000 are still believed to be missing, including over 500 foreigners from more than 30 countries.

The International Red Cross estimated that over 93,000 people have been directly affected by the catastrophe and are in urgent need of humanitarian assistance.

"We're of course very concerned about a secondary flood," said spokesman David Fisher at a press briefing in Geneva, adding that Red Cross relief trucks had been blocked by the lake which formed following the landslide.

Kamal Kishore, Head of the United ​Nations Office for Disaster Risk Reduction, warned of further "cascading hazards that might unfold" and said: "The disaster is ⁠not ​yet completely over. It is still ​unfolding in some ways."

The World Health Organization (WHO) warned of the risk of disease in the wake of the disaster.

"Following a disaster of this scale, displacement, overcrowding ⁠and disruption ​to water, sanitation and health services can increase the risk of infectious diseases, including diarrhoea and respiratory illnesses," said spokesman Tarik ​Jasarevic.

Wednesday's disaster, triggered by a glacial collapse that sent rock and meltwater surging into rivers below, left a new danger in its wake: a barrier lake formed upstream by debris dams. 

China's Ministry of Water Resources said the lake held roughly 2 million cubic meters of water as of Thursday and was expected to receive another 3 million cubic meters — equivalent to about 1,200 Olympic swimming pools — over the following three days, with peak flow expected around September...
body.zh: 红十字会表示，超过 93,000 人受到中尼边境致命洪水和山体滑坡的影响。由于湖水泛滥，可能引发更多洪水，救援工作暂时停止。 尼泊尔和中国边境发生灾难性山洪暴发两天后，救援人员已重新开始搜寻仍失踪的数百人。 周五，由于碎片形成的湖泊开始泛滥，威胁到已经遭受灾难破坏的地区，他们的努力被短暂搁置。 受灾最严重的拉苏瓦地区最高官员纳伦德拉·帕里亚尔 (Narendra Pariyar) 告诉德国之声：“我们收到通知，称该湖已决堤。” “我们可以看到河里的水位正在上升。” 据路透社报道，尼泊尔边境拉苏瓦地区的居民纷纷逃上山坡，以应对河流水位上涨的情况。 当局后来表示，威胁已经缓解，但他们正在密切关注事态发展。 与此同时，尼泊尔表示死亡人数已从一天前的 390 人上升至 579 人。 中国更新了此前西藏三至五人死亡的统计数据。 据信仍有 2,000 多人失踪，其中包括来自 30 多个国家的 500 多名外国人。 国际红十字会估计，超过93,000人直接受到这场灾难的影响，急需人道援助。 发言人大卫·费舍尔在日内瓦举行的新闻发布会上表示：“我们当然非常担心二次洪水。”他补充说，红十字会的救援卡车被山体滑坡后形成的湖泊堵塞。 联合国减少灾害风险办公室主任卡迈勒·基肖尔警告称，“可能会出现更多连锁危险”，并表示：“灾难尚未完全结束。在某些方面，它仍在继续发展。” 世界卫生组织（WHO）就灾难发生后的疾病风险发出警告。 发言人塔里克·贾萨雷维奇 (Tarik Jasarevic) 表示：“如此规模的灾难发生后，流离失所、过度拥挤以及供水、卫生和医疗服务中断可能会增加感染腹泻和呼吸道疾病等传染病的风险。” 周三的灾难是由冰川崩塌引发的，冰川崩塌导致岩石和融水涌入下面的河流，随之而来的是一个新的危险：上游由碎片坝形成的堰塞湖。 中国水利部表示，截至周四，该湖的蓄水量约为 200 万立方米，预计在接下来的三天内将再接收 300 万立方米的水，相当于约 1,200 个奥运游泳池，预计 9 月左右将达到峰值流量。

title.en: How Australians can help those impacted by devastating Nepal floods
title.zh: 澳大利亚人如何帮助受尼泊尔毁灭性洪水影响的人们

summary.en: Australian charities have launched a joint appeal to aid communities devastated by floods and landslides along the Nepal-China border. Thousands are in urgent need of shelter, food, clean water, and medical care after their homes and infrastructure were destroyed.
summary.zh: 澳大利亚慈善机构已发起联合募捐，以援助尼泊尔-中国边境受洪水和山体滑坡摧毁的社区。在房屋和基础设施被毁后，成千上万的人迫切需要住所、食物、清洁饮用水和医疗援助。

body.en:
Entire communities have been devastated by severe flooding and landslides along the Nepal-Tibet border, with homes, roads, bridges and critical infrastructure destroyed.

Search and rescue operations remain underway, while thousands of people are in urgent need of shelter, food, clean drinking water and medical assistance.

In response, 14 Australian charities have joined forces to launch a national appeal.

The Emergency Action Alliance (EAA) has launched the Nepal Flood Disaster Appeal, bringing together a variety of charities to support communities affected by the disaster.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

The alliance says donations will help provide immediate humanitarian assistance, including emergency shelter, food, safe drinking water, hygiene supplies and medical care.

Access to some affected communities remains difficult, with damaged roads and ongoing weather conditions hampering efforts to reach people in need.

Australians are encouraged to donate through the EAA website or by calling 1300 939 000.

The charities participating in the appeal are Save the Children Australia, Plan International Australia, Oxfam Australia, Australia for UNHCR, ActionAid Australia, CARE Australia, Caritas Australia, ADRA, Act for Peace, Anglican Overseas Aid, Australian Lutheran World Service, Baptist World Aid Australia, CBM Australia and Tearfund Australia.

EAA executive director Kerren Morris said the appeal provided Australians with a trusted way to support people affected by the disaster.

"Emergency shelter, food, safe drinking water and medical support are urgently needed now, while longer-term recovery efforts will continue for many months," she said in a statement.

The charities involved bring different areas of humanitarian expertise to the response, with organisations and their local partners working to provide immediate assistance to affected communities.

Save the Children is focusing on supporting children and families affected by humanitarian emergencies.

Oxfam Australia's humanitarian work includes support for essential services such as clean water, sanitation and emergency assistance.

Australia for UNHCR is the UN refugee agency's national partner in Australia, and is supporting humanitarian assistance through the UNHCR network.

The charities involved are continuing to assess the scale of the disaster and humanitarian needs in affected communities.

title.en: Nepal floods: Hundreds killed, over 1,000 missing
title.zh: 尼泊尔洪灾：数百人死亡，一千多人失踪

summary.en: Rescue teams are searching for survivors after a glacial collapse triggered catastrophic floods in Nepal and Tibet. Hundreds of people, including many foreign tourists, are missing.
summary.zh: 救援队正在搜寻幸存者，此前一次冰川崩塌引发了尼泊尔和西藏的灾难性洪水。包括许多外国游客在内的数百人失踪。

body.en:
Rescue teams are searching for survivors after a glacial collapse triggered catastrophic floods in Nepal and Tibet. Hundreds of people, including many foreign tourists, are missing.

The death toll from catastrophic flash floods along the border between  Nepal  and Tibet has risen to at least 392, while more than 1,400 people were missing.

Rescue teams were searching for survivors on Thursday, a day after a glacial collapse sent a huge wall of mud and rock barreling through the Himalayan communities, sweeping away entire villages.

Even with rescue efforts underway, local authorities warned that a fresh disaster could occur as a lake that had formed due to the floodwaters was threatening to burst.

In Tibet, Chinese broadcaster CCTV reported 558 people missing in Gyirong county, including 260 foreigners. Three deaths had been confirmed there as of Thursday morning, with two villagers rescued.

The disaster struck Wednesday when a glacial collapse triggered a flood in the Lhende Khola river, a tributary of the Bhotekoshi, in a corridor popular with trekkers and pilgrims connecting Kathmandu with Lhasa. 

Nepal police spokesperson Abi Narayan Kafle told Reuters the death toll "will go up, as we have resumed the search and more bodies are expected to be recovered."

Neighboring India accounts for the largest proportion of missing foreign nationals. Indian Foreign Minister Subrahmanyam Jaishankar said that 288 Indians were unaccounted for in Nepal, while a further 200 were stranded in China awaiting rescue.

US officials said around 90 US citizens remained unaccounted for on Thursday. The US State Department said three have been rescued, but that it was not yet aware of any deaths among US citizens.

Sunil Sharma, a Nepal tourism board spokesperson, told the AP news agency that many of the missing were pilgrims traveling to Mount Kailash in Tibet, a site sacred to Hindus. In addition to the Indian and US tourists, Sharma said 34 Australians, 33 Britons and 24 Canadians were also missing.

Reuters cited other police and tourism officials who put the missing tourists at 34 from Australia, 33 from Britain and 25 from Canada.

China's Foreign Ministry, meanwhile, said nearly 100 Chinese nationals were unaccounted for. 

During a press conference in Beijing, foreign ministry spokesperson Lin Jian said they were still verifying the breakdown of nationalities of the missing foreigners in Tibet, who were mostly tourists and pilgrims.

China authorities said they were in close communication ‌with Nepal on search and rescue efforts.

Chinese premier Li Qiang has traveled to affected areas in Tibet to view the emergency work, state media reported.

body.zh: 尼泊尔和西藏冰川崩塌引发灾难性洪水后，救援队正在寻找幸存者。数百人失踪，其中包括许多外国游客。 尼泊尔和西藏边境的特大山洪造成的死亡人数已上升至至少 392 人，另有 1,400 多人失踪。 周四，救援队正在寻找幸存者，一天前，冰川崩塌导致一面巨大的泥土和岩石墙穿过喜马拉雅社区，席卷了整个村庄。 尽管救援工作正在进行，但地方当局警告称，由于洪水形成的湖泊有决堤的危险，可能会发生新的灾难。 在西藏，中国中央电视台报道吉隆县有 558 人失踪，其中包括 260 名外国人。截至周四上午，该地区已确认三人死亡，两名村民获救。 灾难于周三发生，冰川崩塌引发博特科希河支流伦德科拉河洪水泛滥，该河是连接加德满都和拉萨的徒步旅行者和朝圣者常去的走廊。 尼泊尔警方发言人阿比·纳拉扬·卡夫勒 (Abi Narayan Kafle) 告诉路透社，死亡人数“将会上升，因为我们已经恢复搜索，预计将找到更多尸体。” 邻国印度在失踪外国人中所占比例最大。印度外交部长苏杰生表示，有 288 名印度人在尼泊尔下落不明，另有 200 人滞留在中国等待救援。 美国官员表示，周四仍有约 90 名美国公民下落不明。美国国务院表示，三人已获救，但尚不清楚有美国公民死亡。 尼泊尔旅游局发言人苏尼尔·夏尔马 (Sunil Sharma) 告诉美联社，许多失踪者是前往西藏冈仁波齐峰的朝圣者，冈仁波齐峰是印度教徒的圣地。夏尔马说，除了印度和美国游客外，还有 34 名澳大利亚人、33 名英国人和 24 名加拿大人失踪。 路透社援引其他警方和旅游官员的话说，失踪的游客中有 34 名来自澳大利亚，33 名来自英国，25 名来自加拿大。 与此同时，中国外交部表示，近100名中国公民下落不明。 外交部发言人林健在北京举行的新闻发布会上表示，他们仍在核实西藏失踪外国人的国籍，这些人主要是游客和朝圣者。 中国当局表示，他们正在与尼泊尔就搜救工作保持密切沟通。 据官方媒体报道，中国总理李强已前往西藏受灾地区查看应急工作。 随着灾难的规模变得...

reflection.en: The earth itself groans under the weight of sin and disaster, as this devastating flood in Nepal and Tibet illustrates. In the midst of such overwhelming loss, we remember that creation itself awaits redemption, and we pray for comfort for those affected and for the eventual renewal of all things.
reflection.zh: 大地本身在罪恶和灾难的重压下呻吟，尼泊尔和西藏这场毁灭性的洪水便是明证。在如此巨大的损失面前，我们当铭记受造之物本身都在等待救赎，并祈求受灾者得到安慰，以及万物终将得到更新。

verse.textEn: We know that the whole creation has been groaning as in the pains of childbirth right up to the present time.
verse.textZh: 我们知道，一切受造之物一同叹息、劳苦，直到如今。

title.en: Number of Australians missing in Nepal floods climbs to 35
title.zh: 尼泊尔洪水和山体滑坡造成数百人失踪，其中包括澳大利亚人

summary.en: Aid workers have described scenes of complete destruction, with entire settlements "wiped out".
summary.zh: 救援人员描述了彻底毁灭的景象，整个定居点“被夷为平地”。

body.en:
The Nepal Tourism Board says 35 Australians are missing after a massive flood and landslide disaster on the Nepal-Tibet border killed at least 273 people on Wednesday, with hundreds more unaccounted for.

That number had been 34 until the tourism board published an update Thursday afternoon.

Another 823 people, including 644 Nepali and foreign tourists, remained out of contact in Nepal, according to the country's disaster agency.

On Thursday afternoon, China's foreign minister said nearly 100 Chinese nationals were missing, revising down earlier reporting in Chinese state media that 558 people, including 260 foreigners, were missing in Gyirong Port, Tibet.

"At this point, there are 34 Australians who are missing," Albanese told a press conference on Thursday morning. "People would have seen some of the footage, which is a truly horrific event."

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

Albanese said it was difficult to obtain information from Nepali authorities and appealed to anyone with information to come forward.

"At this point, Nepal is a developing country. It doesn't have the resources that an event like that would have in Australia, so information is difficult.

"Our thoughts are with all those who will be concerned about their loved ones today."

Defence minister Penny Wong echoed the Prime Minister's statements, noting that the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT) was working "urgently" to ascertain the welfare and location of the missing Australians.

"We are currently deploying further DFAT personnel, including crisis response experts to the region to ensure that we do provide the support needed to these posts, particularly our post in Nepal," Wong in a press conference on Thursday.

"At this stage, access and information are very limited given the scale of disaster. We will do our best, to ascertain whatever information we can."

A US-based tour company Himalayan Glacier Adventures told ABC News that 15 Australians, part of a group of 47 people, were on a hiking tour in the Lantang Valley at the time of the landslides.

The group of Australians was comprised of nine men and six women. Two of those Australians were reportedly boys aged 11 and 14, and a woman aged 64.

Tilak Pokharel, president of the Australian Nepalese Multicultural Centre, said there were "a lot" of people in Melbourne waiting anxiously to hear from loved ones.

"There are a lot of people affected by the flood. There are many people from that area living in Melbourne," Pokharel said.

reflection.en: The news of hundreds missing and entire settlements "wiped out" by floods and landslides in Nepal brings immense sorrow. In moments of such widespread devastation and loss of life, the brevity of "Jesus wept" reminds us that grief is a natural and holy response. Yahweh, in Christ, shares in our human pain, offering a compassionate presence when words fail.
reflection.zh: 尼泊尔洪水和山体滑坡造成数百人失踪、整个定居点“被夷为平地”的消息，带来了巨大的悲痛。在如此大规模的毁灭和生命损失面前，“雅伟哭了”这简短的经文提醒我们，悲伤是一种自然而神圣的回应。雅伟在基督里分担我们人类的痛苦，当言语无法表达时，祂提供了一个充满怜悯的同在。

title.en: WA Labor faces 'tough fight' as One Nation targets historic by-election win
title.zh: 西澳工党面临“一场硬仗”，一国党瞄准历史性补选胜利

summary.en: Recent polling shows support for One Nation has risen in the seat of Secret Harbour, but Labor's vote has remained steady.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及领导、智慧与公共责任。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Labor's stranglehold on the nation's richest state is about to be tested with the rising popularity of One Nation putting a safe seat in doubt.

Voters in the beach-side seat of Secret Harbour, south of Perth, are heading to the polls on Saturday after long-serving MP and senior government minister Paul Papalia's mid-term retirement triggered a state by-election.

"The momentum appears to be with One Nation," political analyst John Phillimore told AAP.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

But the devil could be in the detail, with a recent survey showing support for Labor holding steady at 33 per cent of the primary vote in Western Australia.

One Nation was up three per cent since June, running equal with the Liberals, with 21 per cent of the vote.

"One Nation support is not as high as it is in other parts of the country, so you'd have to be a little bit cautious about calling it early," Phillimore, executive director of Curtin University's John Curtin Institute of Public Policy said.

"By the same token, in a by-election the government was always going to have a big swing against it."

WA Premier Roger Cook concedes it will be a battle to hold the outer suburban, mortgage-belt seat despite Labor's 11.5 per cent margin.

"At the moment, you see a surge on the east coast in popularity of One Nation," he told reporters on Friday.

Cook was also quick to point out that very little rides on the result for his government, which won 46 lower house seats out of 59 in the 2025 state election — the party's third successive landslide victory.

One Nation's performance in tradie-haven Secret Harbour will be of interest across the nation, particularly Victoria, which has a state election in November.

It could have longer-term implications for senior federal Liberal MP Andrew Hastie, whose marginal seat of Canning takes in the Secret Harbour electorate and is being openly targeted by One Nation.

Hastie, considered a future Liberal leader, has vowed to defend the seat which he retained last year on a reduced margin of 6.5 per cent.

One Nation is expected to soon announce a candidate for Canning in the next federal election.
